function.name: lawsuit_search

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph on rural interstates).
• In cities: 25–35 mph; 45 mph on some main streets.
• School zones: 20 mph (or 25 mph if posted). | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must use a child safety seat or booster.
• Back‑seat seats are mandatory for children under 13. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal for adults.
• Lower BAC limits for commercial drivers (0.04 %) and drivers under 21 (0.02 %).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Stop at red lights and stop signs.
• Yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.
• At uncontrolled intersections, yield to vehicles on the right. | | **Headlights & Visibility** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Fog lights are only for foggy conditions. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must display valid registration stickers.
• Towing regulations require proper equipment and safe towing practices. | | **Parking Rules** | • No parking in fire lanes, bus stops, or handicap spaces without proper permits.
• Parking in front of driveways or on sidewalks is prohibited. | | **School Bus Laws** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Drivers must remain stopped until the bus moves again. | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals.
• Do not cut off other vehicles.
• Overtake only when safe and legal. | | **Traffic Cameras & Speed Cameras** | • Texas uses speed cameras in certain counties; fines are issued automatically. | | **Electronic Toll Collection** | • E‑Tag (TxTag) is required for toll roads; failure to pay can result in penalties. | ### How to Stay Updated - **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Official website for current statutes and updates. - **Texas Transportation Code** – Legal text covering all traffic laws. - **Local County Courts** – For specific enforcement policies or recent changes. If you need more detailed information on a particular aspect (e.g., DUI penalties, school bus rules, or toll regulations), let me know!
